title: How can we find a remainder on division by nine?
description: The remainders of four hundred twenty seven and seven thousand three hundred nine on division by nine are found without dividing. Keeko's doubt is that the remainder is thirteen, because the digits add to thirteen.
teaching_notes: One idea: every place value is a multiple of nine plus one, so a number leaves the same remainder as its digit sum. Watch for students who stop at the digit sum and call it the remainder when it is nine or more.

source: Find the remainders of 427 and 7309 on division by 9 without
video_script.why: The student knows a number is a sum of its place values and now sees that each place value leaves remainder one on division by nine.
video_script.substitution: Write each place value as a multiple of nine plus one, collect the multiples of nine, and add the leftover digits.
video_script.anchor: dots in groups of nine, with each place value shown as whole groups of nine and one dot left over
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds the digits four, two and seven to get thirteen and calls it the remainder, forgetting that thirteen holds one more group of nine.
video_script.payoff_line: Four hundred twenty seven leaves remainder four and seven thousand three hundred nine leaves remainder one

final_answer.spoken: four hundred twenty seven leaves remainder four and seven thousand three hundred nine leaves remainder one

maths_rules: 4 + 2 + 7 = 13 = 9 + 4, so the remainder is 4; check 427 = 9 x 47 + 4
7 + 3 + 0 + 9 = 19 = 2 x 9 + 1, so the remainder is 1; check 7309 = 9 x 812 + 1
a remainder on division by 9 is smaller than 9
video_script.design: Each place value is shown as whole groups of nine with one dot left over. The groups of nine are set aside, and the leftover dots are added and regrouped into nines.
